chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And in the hours before dawn they seek forgiveness,' [it is recited] in the Witr prayer at the end of the night, seventy times.

key_terms.الْأَسْحار: The hours before dawn, specifically the last third of the night
key_terms.الْوَتْر: Witr prayer, the odd-numbered prayer offered at night

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of reciting dhikr seventy times in Witr prayer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the practical application of Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:18 by prescribing the recitation of a specific dhikr seventy times during the Witr prayer, highlighting the night's final hours as a prime time for forgiveness. It underscores the Shia emphasis on structured night prayers (Salat al-Layl) and the spiritual discipline of consistent remembrance (dhikr) as a means to attain divine mercy before dawn.
